To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the affinity of a peptide-HLA complex towards the T-cell receptor is linked to its dynamics and to its ability to form intermolecular salt bridges.
the dynamics of p-HLA modulates its recognition by TCR, and that the p-HLA affinity towards TCR is linked to the formation of salt bridges in their ternary complexes.
the dynamics of the HLA head domain and the formation of salt-bridges between the HLA and T-cell receptor are the two key elements that control the immune response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the dynamics of the HLA head and the salt-bridge formation in the recognition of the p-HLA complexes by the TCR.
the dynamics of HLA head sidechains and their role in the immune recognition.
the dynamics of the human leukocyte complex (HLA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p-HLA head dynamics modulates its recognition by the TCR.
, the dynamics of the p-HLA head domain is a crucial factor to determine the immunologic response.
the dynamics of the HLA head is the main factor that controls its reactivity towards TCR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of HLA head domain is a critical factor to determine the immunologic response of a given antigenic peptide.
the dynamics of the HLA head domain modulates its recognition by the T-cell receptor.
HLA dynamics and salt-bridge rearrangements play a key role in the T-cell response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single amino acid change on the antigen can modulate the HLA-TCR interaction, thus affecting T-cell recognition.
the dynamics of the HLA head domain plays a key role in the modulation of the T-cell response.
the HLA head domain is a key component in the T-cell response.
